text:
The Open Door Notes were a series of diplomatic letters sent by U.S. Secretary of State John Hay in 1899–1900, urging major powers to preserve equal trading rights in China and respect its territorial integrity. They aimed to prevent any single nation from monopolizing Chinese markets while keeping China open to all foreign trade. The notes did not create a formal treaty but established the “Open Door Policy” as a guiding principle of U.S. foreign policy in East Asia.
